datasets.name: wikispeedia
datasets.description: Human navigation on Wikipedia: 51,318 finished click trails from the Wikispeedia game, over 4,604 articles. Back clicks are resolved against the browsing history, so each path is the sequence of articles actually visited.

files.name: wikispeedia_paths-and-graph.tar.gz
files.description: Navigation paths and the article hyperlink graph (9.5 MB)

citations: Robert West and Jure Leskovec. Human Wayfinding in Information Networks. WWW, 2012.
Robert West, Joelle Pineau and Doina Precup. Wikispeedia: An Online Game for Inferring Semantic Distances between Concepts. IJCAI, 2009.
datasets.license: Citation requested by SNAP; article content is Wikipedia-derived.

datasets.name: db1b-coupon
datasets.description: US airline itineraries from the BTS Origin and Destination Survey (DB1B), the flight data family behind Rosvall et al. 2014 'Memory in network flows'. A 10% sample of tickets; each itinerary is a sequence of airports (IATA codes) and its weight is the sampled passengers. One quarter per download (~200 MB zip, ~2 GB CSV); pass year= and quarter= to load() for other quarters. Airport coordinates for plotting come from the OpenFlights airports table via .coordinates(); see db1b-city for the same itineraries between metropolitan areas.

files.name: Origin_and_Destination_Survey_DB1BCoupon_2019_1.zip
files.description: Itinerary coupons for 2019 Q1, the default quarter (~202 MB zip)

coordinates.name: airports.dat
coordinates.description: OpenFlights airports table: IATA code, latitude and longitude for ~6,000 airports worldwide (1 MB, Open Database License). Fetched by .coordinates().

citations: Bureau of Transportation Statistics, US Department of Transportation. Origin and Destination Survey DB1BCoupon. https://transtats.bts.gov
datasets.license: US government work, public domain (17 U.S.C. § 105).

datasets.name: db1b-city
datasets.description: The DB1B airline itineraries (see db1b-coupon) at the level of BTS city markets: each node is a metropolitan area's CityMarketID, so JFK, LGA and EWR are one node, and an airport change inside a city collapses to one visit. Reads the very same quarterly coupon archive as db1b-coupon -- the ~200 MB download is shared -- and derives its own path file. Node labels are the ids as strings; .names() maps them to the BTS descriptions, e.g. 31703 -> 'New York City, NY (Metropolitan Area)'.

files.name: Origin_and_Destination_Survey_DB1BCoupon_2019_1.zip
files.description: Itinerary coupons for 2019 Q1, the default quarter (~202 MB zip)

names.name: L_CITY_MARKET_ID.csv
names.description: BTS lookup table L_CITY_MARKET_ID: city market ids and descriptions (Code,Description CSV, ~180 kB; the link's token is BTS's obfuscated table id). Fetched by .names().

citations: Bureau of Transportation Statistics, US Department of Transportation. Origin and Destination Survey DB1BCoupon. https://transtats.bts.gov
